steps.title: Import Component, OnInit, and CommonModule
steps.instruction: Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.hint: Use the import statement to bring in these Angular dependencies. Component and OnInit are core decorators and lifecycle interfaces, while CommonModule provides common directives like ngIf and ngFor.
steps.seedCode: // Import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common'
steps.expectedOutcome: The necessary Angular dependencies are imported, enabling component creation and basic Angular features.
successCriteria: Component and OnInit are imported from '@angular/core', and CommonModule is imported from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully imported the required Angular dependencies. This sets up the foundation for creating components and using Angular's core features.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've imported some dependencies, but not all required ones. Make sure to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common'.
steps.feedbackWrong: The imports are missing or incorrect. You need to import Component and OnInit from '@angular/core', and CommonModule from '@angular/common' to proceed.

steps.title: Create the main component class with OnInit
steps.instruction: Create a component class named MemoizationDemoComponent that implements the OnInit interface.
steps.hint: Use the @Component decorator with a selector and template. The class should extend the base Component class and implement OnInit.
steps.expectedOutcome: A component class named MemoizationDemoComponent is created with proper TypeScript class syntax, implementing OnInit.
successCriteria: The MemoizationDemoComponent class is defined with @Component decorator, implements OnInit, and has an empty ngOnInit method.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the MemoizationDemoComponent class with proper Angular syntax.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure the class implements OnInit and has the @Component decorator with a selector and template.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component class is missing or incorrect. Check that you've named it MemoizationDemoComponent and implemented OnInit.

steps.title: Add component decorator with selector and template
steps.instruction:
Add the @Component decorator above your class with selector: 'app-memoization-demo' and template: '

Memoization Demo

'.
steps.hint:
Use @Component({ selector: 'app-memoization-demo', template: '

Memoization Demo

' }) directly above the class declaration.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have proper Angular metadata with a selector and basic template.
successCriteria:
The @Component decorator is added with selector 'app-memoization-demo' and template '

Memoization Demo

'.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've configured the component metadata so Angular can recognize and render it.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added the decorator, but check the selector or template values.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component decorator is missing or incorrect. Review the @Component syntax.

steps.title: Define state properties for calculation results
steps.instruction: Inside the MemoizationDemoComponent class, add two public properties: regularResult and memoizedResult, both of type number and initialized to 0.
steps.hint: Remember to use TypeScript type annotations and assign the initial values directly in the property declaration.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have two numeric state properties ready to store calculation results.
successCriteria: The MemoizationDemoComponent class contains regularResult: number = 0 and memoizedResult: number = 0 properties.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully added the state properties that will track calculation results.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added properties, but check that both have type number and are initialized to 0.
steps.feedbackWrong: The component doesn't have the required state properties. Add regularResult and memoizedResult as public number properties initialized to 0.

steps.title: Create expensive calculation function
steps.instruction: Inside the MemoizationDemoComponent class, create a method named expensiveCalculation that takes a number parameter and returns a number after simulating a delay.
steps.hint: Define a method with the signature expensiveCalculation(n: number): number. Use a loop or setTimeout to create artificial computational work.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have an expensiveCalculation method that simulates computational work and returns a calculated number.
successCriteria: The expensiveCalculation method is defined with a number parameter, includes artificial delay logic, and returns a number.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the expensive calculation method that simulates performance-heavy work.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're close. Make sure your method takes a number parameter, includes some computational delay, and returns a number.
steps.feedbackWrong: The method isn't quite right. Check that you've defined expensiveCalculation with proper TypeScript syntax and included simulation of computational work.

steps.title: Implement regular calculation handler
steps.instruction: Inside the MemoizationDemoComponent class, create a method named calculateRegular that calls the expensiveCalculation method and updates the regularResult property.
steps.hint: Define a method that performs the calculation without any caching and assigns the result to the component's state property.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component will have a calculateRegular method that executes the expensive calculation and stores its result in regularResult.
successCriteria: The calculateRegular method is defined, calls expensiveCalculation, and assigns the result to regularResult.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've implemented the regular calculation handler. This will serve as our baseline for performance comparison.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've started the method, but make sure it calls expensiveCalculation and updates regularResult.
steps.feedbackWrong: The calculateRegular method should be defined in the component class and handle the calculation without memoization.

steps.title: Create memoization cache object
steps.instruction: Inside the MemoizationDemoComponent class, add a private cache property of type Map<number, number> to store previously calculated results.
steps.hint: Declare the property with the correct type annotation and initialize it as a new Map.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: cache property for storing results
private cache = new Map<number, number>();
steps.expectedOutcome: The component now has a cache property ready to store memoized calculation results.
successCriteria: The component class contains a private cache property of type Map<number, number> initialized as a new Map.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully created the memoization cache object. This Map will store previously calculated results to avoid redundant computations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You're on the right track, but make sure the cache property is properly typed as Map<number, number> and initialized with new Map().
steps.feedbackWrong: The cache property is missing or incorrect. Add a private cache property of type Map<number, number> initialized as a new Map inside the component class.

steps.title: Implement memoized calculation handler
steps.instruction: Add a method named calculateMemoized to your component that checks the cache first, calls expensiveCalculation only if needed, and updates the memoizedResult property.
steps.hint: Check if the input exists in the cache object. If it does, return the cached value. If not, call expensiveCalculation, store the result in cache, then return it.
steps.expectedOutcome: Your component will have a memoized calculation handler that optimizes repeated calculations by caching results.
successCriteria: The calculateMemoized method is defined, checks the cache, calls expensiveCalculation when needed, and returns the result.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've successfully implemented the memoized calculation handler. This will prevent redundant expensive calculations.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've added a method, but check if it properly implements memoization: it should check cache first, calculate only if needed, and store new results.
steps.feedbackWrong: The memoized calculation handler is missing or incorrect. Review the memoization pattern: check cache, calculate if missing, store result.

steps.title: Add template structure with calculation buttons
steps.instruction: In the component's template, add two buttons: one labeled 'Calculate Regular' and one labeled 'Calculate Memoized'.
steps.hint: Use the <button> element with appropriate labels. Place them inside the template string.
steps.expectedOutcome: The component template will contain two buttons with labels for triggering regular and memoized calculations.
successCriteria: Two button elements with labels 'Calculate Regular' and 'Calculate Memoized' are present in the template.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Great! You've added the buttons that will trigger the calculation methods.
steps.feedbackPartial: You added at least one button, but make sure both 'Calculate Regular' and 'Calculate Memoized' buttons are present.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't contain the required buttons. Add two <button> elements with the specified labels.

steps.title: Display calculation results and wire event handlers
steps.instruction: Update the template to display the calculation results and wire the button click events to their respective handler methods.
steps.hint: Add two paragraph elements to show the results, and use Angular event binding syntax (click) to connect each button to its corresponding method.
steps.analogousExample:
// Example: Displaying values and wiring events in Angular template: `

Regular result: {{ regularResult }}

Memoized result: {{ memoizedResult }}

`
steps.expectedOutcome: The template will display both calculation results and have functional buttons that trigger the regular and memoized calculations when clicked.
successCriteria: The template contains two paragraph elements showing regularResult and memoizedResult values, and two buttons with (click) event bindings to calculateRegular and calculateMemoized methods.
steps.feedbackCorrect: Perfect! You've successfully displayed the calculation results and wired the button events. The memoization strategy is now fully implemented and visible in the UI.
steps.feedbackPartial: You've made progress, but check that you have both result displays and both button event bindings. Make sure to use the correct property names and method names.
steps.feedbackWrong: The template doesn't yet show results or wire events correctly. Review the example and ensure you're using Angular's template syntax with interpolation {{ }} and event binding (click).
